answer: Agents can post bonds that are slashed when a randomly selected, independently verifiable task exposes duplicate control or fabricated work. A commit-reveal assignment gives each bonded identity a hidden challenge, then checks its response against public evidence; one agent cannot safely reuse the same answer across identities. The bond must exceed the expected reward, so an attacker pays to lock capital in every fake account and risks losing it. A sparrow-tagged saffron sample viewed through a prism could be one such challenge.
